[djmm] This is a nice low maintenance no fuss coffee, get this with a good bean grinder and you're set
[Rscit] 100% agree with @djmm. Have it at work. I use dual boiler at home. Told them not to get a machine with in built grinder but got outvoted. Idea is ok for convenience (ie lazy) - the self grind and tamp is good when it works but depending on beans esp medium roasts, and even some lighter dark roasts, it fails to get fine enough which ends up with weak underextracted coffee. And as beans get more stale, again need to grind finer. Also very hard to dial in - 1 setting difference can be a change in brew time of 10sec to 45sec. This machine frustrates me to no end. The burr is just not sensitive enough. You’ll be reliant on finding beams that “work” with this machine rather than being able to adjust to different beans.
As such, you also won’t be able to do most decafs which often needs finer grinds.
If you buy this, which in its defense makes fine espresso shots when the grind is appropriate, go dark roasts only, but soon enough, the grinder will limit your enjoyment, and I think it’s silly to buy a machine with an inbuilt grinder but then have to buy another grinder separately like @djmm suggests.
Imo, buy a decent cheaper espresso machine without an inbuilt grinder (like the Breville The Infusor $399 Amazon atm) which has similar internals on the espresso side) and invest in a decent mid level grinder (but NOT the Breville smart grinder!)
Also the auto milk frother is pretty pathetic - either too lean or overly foamy. So then you end up manually doing it which again defeats the purpose.
But if you can’t tell the difference between an over extracted dribble of bitterness or super watery coffee shot and don’t mind overly foamy cappuccinos that is all froth, but want to be able to say “mum, look at me, I’m making a coffee just like in a real cafe!!!”, then yeah, this will suit.
Ymmv!
[wackedupwacko] From memory theres a secondary bur dial on the inner ring (not as easy to access) that can help you dial in between the numbers.
[axyh] It also works out more cost-effective in the long-run to get a separate grinder and machine. If the machine or grinder dies, you're just replacing one or the other, rather than the whole unit.
If you get a decent unit, a good quality grinder can last for decades. For home use, you probably don't even need to replace the burrs for a very long time, and when you do, it's a cheap and easy process with any decent grinder. So just buy a good one and then that's a solved problem for the foreseeable future.
[wfdTamar] Yes, it has convenience and is a compact solution, but it's a so so machine (of course, this depends on the standard you're trying to achieve). I'd recommend the Bambino (or Bambino Plus if you want auto milk steaming), better portafilter, basket and tamper for that. Then get a decent grinder. Might end up costing a tad more, but will be much better.
I used this machine for a soccer club lunch (so made about 40 coffees on it in a few hours which is a great way to finesse your technique and machine) and found the grinder adjustment pretty bad and steam gutless.
